en.commentary:
I ranked these ten travel eSIMs on one question: what does a 30-day trip to Japan cost, and does the provider tell you, before you pay, exactly where the fast data stops and which network you will ride on?

Price per GB leads my scoring because it is the one number every provider can be compared on. On a 10GB, 30-day Japan plan, Nomad is $16 on sale, Jetpac is $16, Ubigi is $16.50, Saily is $17.99 and aloSIM is $18. That spread is only two dollars, so the tiebreakers decide the order.

The tiebreaker I weight most is fair-use disclosure. Every "unlimited" plan I checked has a daily threshold, and the good providers print it. Ubigi says 60GB at full speed, then 2 Mbps. Airalo says 3GB a day, then 1 Mbps. Jetpac says 3GB a day, then up to 1 Mbps. Maya Mobile says 5GB a day, then 3 Mbps. Holafly's Japan page states the carrier may slow speeds for up to a day and points to its terms for the exact threshold, so it scores lowest on this column.

Ubigi takes first place. It names KDDI and NTT Docomo on the plan page, allows data sharing, and gives you six months to activate. Nomad is a hair behind with KDDI au and SoftBank named and add-on data that attaches to the same eSIM. Jetpac earns third with unlimited tethering and a lounge pass when your flight is delayed more than an hour.

Airalo, past 30 million customers, is my pick for the traveler who wants unlimited in Japan with a published policy, at $69 for 30 days. One disclosure for readers of my VPN ranking: Saily is run by Nord Security, the same company behind NordVPN.

highlights.title: Ubigi wins because its plan page answers every question before checkout
highlights.body: Ubigi's Japan 10GB plan is $16.50 for 30 days, and the same page names KDDI and NTT Docomo, confirms data sharing, and gives a six-month activation window. Its unlimited Japan plan states 60GB at full speed, then 2 Mbps, which is the most generous published threshold I found. I can buy it a month before a Tokyo trip and know exactly what I will get when I land at Narita.

highlights.title: The published throttle number is the most useful spec in this category
highlights.body: An unlimited plan is only as good as its daily threshold. Airalo publishes 3GB a day then 1 Mbps, Jetpac 3GB then up to 1 Mbps, Maya Mobile 5GB then 3 Mbps, and Ubigi 60GB then 2 Mbps. I scored fair-use disclosure as its own column because a traveler streaming Google Maps and Instagram all day hits 3GB by mid-afternoon, and the number printed on the page tells you whether dinner will load.

highlights.title: Jetpac is the best-value extra in travel eSIMs
highlights.body: At $16 for 10GB over 30 days, Jetpac already ties for the cheapest mainstream Japan month. It adds unlimited tethering and SmartDelay: register your flight up to 24 hours before departure, and a delay of more than an hour sends you and a companion a LoungeKey pass. One delayed evening flight makes that perk worth more than the plan itself.

highlights.title: Maya Mobile is the heavy user's unlimited plan
highlights.body: Maya Mobile charges $49.99 for 30 days in Japan with 5GB of high-speed data every day and 3 Mbps after that, with hotspot included. For someone tethering a laptop, that is about $0.33 per GB of fast data, and 3 Mbps keeps video calls usable after the cap. It is the unlimited plan I would buy for a working trip.

highlights.title: Holafly is the simple buy, and simplicity carries a price
highlights.body: Holafly's Japan unlimited plan costs $73.90 for 30 days on KDDI and SoftBank, with 1GB of daily hotspot sharing and a 1GB monthly backup in 150+ countries. It suits travelers who want to pick a number of days and never think about data again. For a clearly written threshold at a lower price, Airalo's $69 plan and Maya's $49.99 plan both deliver more.

zh-tw.commentary:
這份榜單我只問一件事：去日本玩 30 天，要花多少錢，還有付錢之前，商家有沒有把高速流量在哪裡停、走哪家電信講清楚。

每 GB 價格是我評分的第一順位，因為這是唯一能跨品牌直接比的數字。以日本 10GB、30 天來算，Nomad 特價 16 美元、Jetpac 16 美元、Ubigi 16.50 美元、Saily 17.99 美元、aloSIM 18 美元。差距只有兩美元左右，換成台幣大概一杯超商咖啡，所以名次其實是由其他欄位決定的。

我最看重的是公平使用政策有沒有寫出來。說真的，我查過的「吃到飽」全部都有每日門檻，差別只在有沒有老實寫。Ubigi 寫 60GB 全速後 2 Mbps，Airalo 寫每天 3GB 後 1 Mbps，Jetpac 寫每天 3GB 後最高 1 Mbps，Maya Mobile 寫每天 5GB 後 3 Mbps。Holafly 的日本頁面寫的是電信商可能限速最多一天，確切門檻放在條款裡，所以這一欄它拿全榜最低分。

第一名我給 Ubigi，很有把握。方案頁直接寫出 KDDI 跟 NTT Docomo，可以分享熱點，買完六個月內啟用都行，出發前一個月先買好完全沒壓力。Nomad 只差一點點，寫明 KDDI au 跟 SoftBank，加購流量會自動接在同一張 eSIM 上。Jetpac 拿第三，熱點不設限，班機延誤超過一小時還送貴賓室。

想在日本用吃到飽、又要看得到明文規則，我推 Airalo，30 天 69 美元。最後提醒一下看過我 VPN 榜的朋友，Saily 是 Nord Security 經營的，跟 NordVPN 同一家母公司。

highlights.title: Ubigi 第一，因為結帳前你想問的它都寫了
highlights.body: 日本 10GB、30 天 16.50 美元，同一頁寫出 KDDI 跟 NTT Docomo、確認可以分享熱點，買完六個月內啟用都有效。吃到飽方案寫明前 60GB 全速、之後 2 Mbps，這是我查到最大方的明文門檻。老實說，出發前一個月在台灣買好，落地成田就知道自己會拿到什麼，這種安心感很值錢。

highlights.title: 降速門檻寫出來，是這個品類最有用的規格
highlights.body: 吃到飽好不好用，看的是每日門檻。Airalo 每天 3GB 後 1 Mbps、Jetpac 3GB 後最高 1 Mbps、Maya Mobile 5GB 後 3 Mbps、Ubigi 60GB 後 2 Mbps。我把這欄獨立出來評分，因為整天開 Google Maps 導航、狂發 IG 限動，下午三點左右就會用掉 3GB，晚上要查餐廳時網路順不順，就看頁面上寫的那個數字。

highlights.title: Jetpac 的附加價值是全榜最實在的
highlights.body: 10GB、30 天 16 美元，本來就並列主流品牌最便宜的日本月方案，熱點還不設限。再加上 SmartDelay，起飛前 24 小時登記航班，延誤超過一小時就送你跟同行者 LoungeKey 貴賓室。說真的，碰上一次晚班機延誤，這個福利就比方案本身還值錢。

highlights.title: 重度使用者的吃到飽，我選 Maya Mobile
highlights.body: 日本 30 天 49.99 美元，每天 5GB 高速，用完降到 3 Mbps，熱點照樣能開。拿手機分享給筆電工作的人，算下來每 GB 高速流量約 0.33 美元，降速後 3 Mbps 開視訊會議還撐得住。要帶筆電去日本出差或當數位遊牧，我會買這張。

highlights.title: Holafly 買的是省事，省事本身就要付錢
highlights.body: 日本吃到飽 30 天 73.90 美元，約台幣 2,300 元，走 KDDI 跟 SoftBank，熱點每天可分享 1GB，另送每月 1GB 的全球備用流量。只想選天數、完全不管流量的人，它最方便。想要規則寫得清楚又便宜一點，Airalo 的 69 美元跟 Maya 的 49.99 美元都給得更多。

en.commentary:
The eSIM market crossed a real inflection point in 2026, industry forecasts now put global travel eSIM users at over 215 million by 2028, up from 40 million in 2024, and multiple new comparison reports published this month confirm what I've found in my own testing: pricing discipline and fair-use policy matter more than headline data allowances.

Ubigi keeps the top spot because its fair-use policy is the most generous and transparently stated in this entire category, a 9.5 score, combined with the strongest network partnerships score of 9.5. When I need an eSIM that just works across multiple countries without throttling surprises, Ubigi is still what I reach for.

Nomad holds second because its pricing remains the sharpest in the category at 9.3, and its network score matches Ubigi's. The tradeoff is a slightly less polished app, but the core service is excellent.

Jetpac remains third on the strength of the best hotspot-sharing score in this list at 9.5, if you're traveling with a group and need to share one data plan across multiple devices, Jetpac handles it better than anything else here.

A widely cited value index published this month found that travelers often overpay by choosing inflexible plan durations, which reinforces why I keep weighting fair-use and pricing flexibility as heavily as I do.

No single provider news justifies a rank change this cycle, so today's entry carries the board forward unchanged.

highlights.body: A 9.5 fair-use score paired with the strongest network partnerships in this list. When I need an eSIM that just works across multiple countries without throttling surprises, this is still it.

highlights.title: Nomad's pricing is the sharpest, with network coverage to match
highlights.body: A 9.3 price score and a network score tied with Ubigi's. The app is a little less polished, but the core service more than makes up for it.

highlights.title: Jetpac still wins for group travel hotspot sharing
highlights.body: The best hotspot score in this list at 9.5. If you're splitting one data plan across a group's devices, nothing here handles it better.

zh-tw.commentary:
eSIM 市場在 2026 年真的走到一個轉折點,產業預測全球旅遊 eSIM 用戶到 2028 年會超過 2.15 億,從 2024 年的 4000 萬一路成長上來,這個月又有好幾份新的比較報告出爐,結果都印證了我自己實測的心得,定價透明度跟公平使用政策,比表面上的流量數字更重要。

Ubigi 繼續第一,它的公平使用政策在這個類別裡最寬鬆也最透明,拿到 9.5 分,加上網路涵蓋合作夥伴分數也是 9.5,同樣頂尖。每次我需要一張能跨多國穩定使用、不會突然被限速的 eSIM,還是會選 Ubigi。

Nomad 維持第二,定價在整個類別裡最精準,拿下 9.3 分,網路分數跟 Ubigi 打平。唯一的取捨是 APP 體驗稍微沒那麼精緻,但核心服務品質很扎實。

Jetpac 維持第三,靠的是榜單裡最強的熱點分享分數 9.5 分,如果你是跟一群人出國,需要一張卡分享給多台裝置用,Jetpac 在這方面做得比誰都好。

這個月被廣泛引用的一份價值指數報告指出,旅客常常因為選了不夠彈性的方案天數而多花冤枉錢,這也印證了我為什麼一直把公平使用政策跟定價彈性看得這麼重。

這波沒有單一業者的新聞強到需要調整名次,今天的排名維持原樣。

en.commentary:
eSIM adoption just crossed another real milestone, Juniper Research puts total eSIM devices at 1.2 billion in 2025, with growth projected around 30 percent through 2026 alone. That is a faster curve than most connectivity categories see, and it explains why the field keeps getting crowded with new entrants promising cheap data and simple activation. The volume of new comparison coverage this month also confirms something I keep testing myself, headline gigabyte counts are easy to advertise and easy to get wrong about, fair-use throttling and hotspot restrictions are where most travelers actually get burned.

Ubigi keeps the top spot because its fair-use policy disclosure remains the clearest in this category at a 9.5 score, travelers know exactly what happens before they hit a data ceiling, not finding out mid trip. Nomad holds rank two on a 9.3 price score paired with the same 9.5 named network transparency, a combination that keeps it the best value pick for anyone prioritizing predictable Japan pricing over app polish. Airalo's 9.5 app score keeps it relevant at rank four even with a weaker 6.5 price score, proof that a smooth top-up experience still earns real loyalty despite costing more per gigabyte.

As adoption keeps climbing toward 2028 projections of over 200 million travel eSIM users, I expect fair-use transparency to keep separating the winners here more than raw price ever will.

zh-tw.commentary:
eSIM 的普及又跨過一個實際的里程碑，Juniper Research 統計2025年全球 eSIM 裝置數量已經到12億台，預估光是2026年成長率就有約30%。這個成長曲線比大多數連網相關類別都快，也解釋了為什麼這個市場一直有新品牌搶進來，主打便宜流量跟簡單開通。這個月大量的比較報導也再次驗證我自己實測時一直發現的事，主打的流量吉位數字很好打廣告，但也很容易誤導消費者，真正讓旅客踩雷的往往是公平使用限速跟熱點分享的限制。

Ubigi 能繼續守住第一名，是因為它的公平使用政策揭露在這個類別裡還是最清楚的，拿到9.5分，旅客在出發前就能確切知道流量上限在哪裡，不用等旅途中才發現被限速。Nomad 能守住第二名，靠的是9.3的價格分數，再加上同樣9.5的當地電信商透明標示，這個組合讓它成為在意日本價格可預期性、勝過在意 App 介面好不好用的旅客最佳選擇。Airalo 即使價格分數只有6.5分，還是靠9.5的 App 體驗分數守住第四名，證明順暢的加購流量體驗還是能換來真實的忠誠度，就算每 GB 比較貴。

隨著採用率持續往2028年預估的兩億多旅遊用 eSIM 用戶邁進，我預期公平使用透明度接下來會比單純比價格，更能拉開這份榜單裡贏家跟其他人的差距。

highlights.title: eSIM 裝置數突破12億台
highlights.body: Juniper Research 統計2025年全球 eSIM 裝置達12億台，預估2026年成長率約30%，比多數連網類別都快。

en.commentary: Ubigi keeps the top spot today on the same 9.5 network score and 9.5 fair use policy that have anchored it here for weeks, no hidden throttling buried in fine print the way some unlimited plans hide it. Nomad holds a close second, and its new Nomad Pass subscription, $3 a month that auto renews 1GB every 30 days, is quietly one of the smarter product moves in this category this year, a baseline safety net for anyone who travels often enough to want connectivity without re-buying a plan every single trip. I want to spend today's entry on Airalo, which sits fifth overall but still carries the highest app score in this ranking at 9.5. That matters more than it sounds for a first time eSIM buyer: the installation flow, QR code scanning, and plan switching inside Airalo's app is simply the easiest onboarding experience in this category, which is exactly why it remains the eSIM I recommend to someone trying this for the very first time even though its 6.5 price score is the second lowest here. Saily backs that up with a 9.0 app score of its own, Nord Security's design language carries over cleanly from the VPN world. For anyone price sensitive and willing to tolerate a rougher interface, Ubigi, Nomad, and Jetpac still win on pure cost per gigabyte, Jetpac's 9.5 hotspot score is also worth flagging for anyone tethering a laptop on the road. My overall take hasn't shifted: Ubigi and Nomad for value focused travelers who know what they're doing, Airalo for first timers who want the easiest possible setup.
